about.title: North Hollywood Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: North Hollywood, part of Los Angeles County's dense healthcare landscape, is home to numerous urgent care centers, imaging clinics, and outpatient surgical practices along Lankershim and Victory Boulevard. When care at one of these facilities falls short of accepted medical standards, patients are often left with new injuries, extended recovery, or worsened conditions. Medical malpractice claims are not simply about a bad result — California law requires showing that a provider deviated from the standard of care and that deviation caused harm. Because these cases hinge on medical records, expert review, and strict procedural steps, patients in North Hollywood benefit from having an attorney evaluate what happened early on. We don't charge you upfront to review your situation; our team can assess your circumstances, explain your options under California's malpractice rules, and help you understand what a path forward might look like given your specific case.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a California Medical Malpractice Case

items.title: Strict Filing Windows
items.desc: California generally requires a claim within one year of discovering the injury, and no more than three years from when it occurred. Missing either deadline can end a claim before it starts, so early attorney review matters.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit against a healthcare provider, California law requires sending a formal 90-day notice of intent. We help make sure this step is handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: Because a bad medical outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, California cases typically need a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached. Our team works with the process of securing that kind of review.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery in North Hollywood — does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard and that this specifically caused your injury. We can help review your medical records to see whether that standard was actually breached.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim against a North Hollywood hospital or clinic?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from when it happened. There's also a required 90-day pre-suit notice before filing, so timing matters a great deal here.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover in a California malpractice case?
items.answer: California caps non-economic damages in medical malpractice cases, though that cap rises annually under state law. Economic damages like medical bills and lost income are generally handled separately. We can walk you through how these categories might apply to your situation.
